transcript: Welcome to the 2024.2 new feature videos. In this video we will look at Advanced Pinching with Soft Selection. For control of the cloth and detailed simulation, a soft selection function has been added as an advanced pinching option. In order to activate soft selection, the Select and Move tool has to be activated while simulation is active. By right-clicking 3D Window, you can find Advanced Pinching option. You can also press Shift-E as a shortcut. When you activate the Advanced Pinching option, a new window will pop up on screen. There's two different sections on this pop-up window. On top, you'll see a Range section, providing options for Falloff Shape, Falloff Distance, and Falloff Power. Below that is an Options section, providing options for Distance Measure, Distance Indicator, Limit to a Selected Patterns, and Display Weights. By default, the Distance Indicator is turned on, and you will see a selection range as two concentric circles. The inner circle indicates Falloff Power, and the outer circle indicates Falloff Distance. Let's toggle on the Display Weights option. When Display Weights is activated, the selection range will be displayed in green. Falloff Shape provides Bump and Linear options. Bump has relatively wide range of selection range. Linear, on the other hand, has a tighter range of selection. Let's adjust the Falloff Distance and Falloff Power to the Max value to see a clearer visual difference. With a Linear option, the range selected is tighter. With a Bump option, on the other hand, you can see that the wider range is selected. I will set everything back to default values. Distance Measure provides two different options, Surface and Straight. When you set it to Surface, the selection is happening along the surface from the center point of your indicator. Your selection is limited to a single layer pattern. When Straight is selected, you can select everything in the 3D space, where Distance Indicator covers. This allows you to select multiple layers in the scene. When Limit to Selected Patterns box is checked, your selection is limited within a selected pattern, no matter what you choose in Distance Measure option. This will be useful when you want to fix the clothes that are sticking each other as you simulate.
summary: # Marvelous Designer 2024.2: Advanced Pinching With Soft Selection ## Introduction Welcome to the 2024.2 new feature videos. In this video, we will look at Advanced Pinching with Soft Selection. ## Overview of Soft Selection For control of the cloth and detailed simulation, a soft selection function has been added as an advanced pinching option. To activate soft selection, the Select and Move tool must be activated while simulation is active. ## Activating Advanced Pinching To find the Advanced Pinching option, right-click in the 3D Window. You can also press **Shift + E** as a shortcut. When you activate the Advanced Pinching option, a new window will pop up on the screen. ### Pop-Up Window Sections There are two different sections on this pop-up window: 1. **Range Section**: This section provides options for: - Falloff Shape - Falloff Distance - Falloff Power 2. **Options Section**: This section provides options for: - Distance Measure - Distance Indicator - Limit to Selected Patterns - Display Weights By default, the Distance Indicator is turned on, and you will see a selection range represented as two concentric circles. The inner circle indicates Falloff Power, while the outer circle indicates Falloff Distance. ## Display Weights Let's toggle on the Display Weights option. When Display Weights is activated, the selection range will be displayed in green. ## Falloff Shape Options The Falloff Shape provides two options: **Bump** and **Linear**. - **Bump** has a relatively wide range of selection. - **Linear**, on the other hand, has a tighter range of selection. ### Adjusting Falloff Values Let's adjust the Falloff Distance and Falloff Power to the maximum value to see a clearer visual difference. With the Linear option, the range selected is tighter. In contrast, with the Bump option, you can see that a wider range is selected. I will set everything back to default values. ## Distance Measure Options The Distance Measure provides two different options: **Surface** and **Straight**. - When you set it to **Surface**, the selection occurs along the surface from the center point of your indicator, and your selection is limited to a single layer pattern. - When **Straight** is selected, you can select everything in the 3D space that the Distance Indicator covers. This allows you to select multiple layers in the scene. ## Limiting Selections When the **Limit to Selected Patterns** box is checked, your selection is limited within a selected pattern, regardless of what you choose in the Distance Measure option. This feature will be useful when you want to fix the clothes that are sticking to each other as you simulate.
